claims.text: The baseline TaNbVTi refractory alloy has a single BCC solid-solution microstructure.
The baseline alloy is produced by powder metallurgy.
The baseline receives conventional heat treatment and has typical impurity levels.
Introducing approximately 0.2 molar fraction Al into TaNbVTi improves its high-temperature mechanical performance.
Al addition reduces the alloy's density.
Al addition retains satisfactory room-temperature ductility.
Al induces fine, uniformly distributed, coherent precipitates within the BCC matrix.
The Al-induced particles may be lightly ordered sigma or other coherent intermetallic phases.
Al alters phase stability during heat treatment so that fine precipitates form.
The Al-modified alloy retains a BCC solid-solution matrix.
Fine precipitates impede dislocation motion at high temperature.
Precipitate obstruction increases high-temperature yield strength and creep resistance.
A retained solid solution and controlled precipitate volume prevent degradation of room-temperature properties.
Relative to unalloyed TaNbVTi, the Al-modified alloy will improve high-temperature yield strength by approximately 10–20%.
Relative to unalloyed TaNbVTi, the Al-modified alloy will improve creep resistance by approximately 10–20%.
The Al-modified alloy will maintain room-temperature yield strength and ductility similar to the baseline.
TaNbVTi-based RHEAs can retain measurable specific strength at 900 °C and 1200 °C.
The unalloyed TaNbVTi baseline suffers softening at high operating temperatures.
Al contents well above 0.2 molar fraction may cause excessive precipitation or embrittlement and degrade room-temperature ductility.
The beneficial Al effect is restricted to a narrow compositional window.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes Al as substituting for a portion of the refractory elements, whereas the experiment describes Al as being added; these routes imply different normalized compositions unless the formulation is clarified.

The proposed strengthening mechanism requires a precipitate-containing microstructure, but the cited same-system record reports a single BCC solid solution and attributes the properties of TaNbVTiAl0.2 to uniform microstructure and solid-solution strengthening.
